nodes.title: Tube wall + LE fillet zone modulus 3 GPa
nodes.text: Isotropic 3 GPa (nu 0.35) for the zone between the square bar face and the board LE (tube wall + epoxy fillet)
nodes.basis: Stands in for the shell model's rigid LE link: 100x stiffer in shear than the paper faces over 5.7 mm, adds 0.6 % to the tube's out-of-plane EI

nodes.title: D5 shoe region modulus 50 GPa (rigid)
nodes.text: Shoe legs, cheeks, glue and the board inside them as one stiff isotropic block (50 GPa), as the shell model's rigid shoe
nodes.basis: Same idealisation as fin_fe rigid_fin. The two legs are joined by the sleeve floor on the step edge and by the back wall, so the board between them cannot shear or bend freely: the block is the closer of the two simple models. C4-R6 (CDR-01 e) tried the other one, legs only at the PETG modulus (1.5 GPa x 0.8 / 1.0 mm in the outer layers, board left as board, mesh_quarter shoe_mode 'petg'): without the sleeve tie the 7 mm legs peel off the faces and the face stress is 72 MPa limit on mesh level 1, which is not the load path of the part as built. A model with the sleeve as a 3-D body is not built; the rigid block stays the upper bound on the stress jump at the leg edge

nodes.title: Modal model: 7 mm of each shoe leg counted as rigid, as before D-106
nodes.text: In the station-mode model the rigid shoe block reaches 7 mm below the step (|z| 0.194), not the 30 mm of the legs as drawn; the leg mass is in the foot mass (CL-D5-MASS-FOOT)
nodes.basis: a rigid block over the full 30 mm legs stiffens the fin tip in a way two 0.8 mm PETG skins cannot (see ASM-C4-SHOE-Z0); the face-stress model keeps the full legs

nodes.title: Shoe free corner on the board rounded R 0.5 mm
nodes.text: The corner of each shoe leg / cheek outline that ends on the bare board is a 0.5 mm radius in the planform mesh
nodes.basis: CDR-ST-17: a 0.4 mm nozzle cannot print a sharper outside corner (D5 FEA uses R 0.4 for the same reason); with the epoxy squeeze-out the real corner is blunter. Resolved by about 2 elements on the finest mesh

nodes.title: Station-collar tail tongue modulus 1 GPa (PETG, 45 % fill)
nodes.text: Isotropic 1 GPa (nu 0.35) for the printed tail tongue that replaces the board in the notched LE-top corner, from the tube surface to 40 mm aft, strip band + 1 mm deep; the CF edge strips run on over it to the tube
nodes.basis: PETG about 2.0 GPa solid x P:fin_detail.station_collar.tongue_fill 0.45 (perimeters carry more): 1 GPa. The R4 shell model had the strips ending on a rigid LE link; the first 3-D pass ended them at the board LE and put 26 MPa into the paper faces at the LE (artefact, removed by this zone)

nodes.title: Hot-spot read distances 0.4 t and 1.0 t, t = laminate 9.6 mm
nodes.text: Face stress at the shoe edge = linear surface extrapolation from 0.4 t and 1.0 t (IIW type a), t = two-board laminate thickness
nodes.basis: the peak at a rigid-insert edge is singular and grows with mesh refinement; the hot-spot value converges and is the structural stress the faces carry

nodes.title: As-designed station masses: motor 84.2 g, ESC 7.6 g, bullets 4 g
nodes.text: A3-R6a roll-up items: PRP-001 motor with its four M3 screws 84.2 g (params 81 g), PRP-002 stripped ESC 7.6 g (params 6.6 g), HRN-E03 phase bullets and short leads 4 g at 0.8 z_st on the tube

nodes.title: Benchmark tip load 10 N on the 100 x 10 x 10 mm two-modulus cantilever
nodes.text: Solver benchmark only (not aircraft data): steel/aluminium halves, 10 N tip shear

nodes.title: SU2 ELASTICITY cantilever benchmark, 3 meshes
nodes.equation: tip deflection, 10 N tip shear on a 100 x 10 x 10 mm cantilever, E 70/210 GPa halves; reference d = P (7 L^3/(24 E1 I) + L^3/(24 E2 I)) + P L/(k G A), k = 5/6; meshes 2/4/8 elements through the depth (aspect 1); Richardson on the three; hex8 in-house on the same meshes

nodes.title: SU2 ELASTICITY on the fin quarter: solver trials against the hex8 direct solve
nodes.equation: upper quarter, mesh level 1 (8 mm / 2 mm, 71 k DOF), D5 shoe as drawn, L4 side part; SU2 v8 linear solvers available in this build (no PaStiX): CG + ILU(1) and restarted FGMRES(200) + ILU(2), 1500 it each, tol 1e-9; converged when log10 residual <= -6; field difference max |u_hex - u_su2| / max |u_hex|

nodes.title: Fin face hot-spot stress at the D5 shoe, SU2, 3 meshes
nodes.equation: hex8 direct solve (identical to SU2 ELASTICITY, CALC-C4-SIM-CODES); L4 limit: F = (-F_corner, +/- max(mu F_corner, F_C5), 0) at the C1 ground point through the rigid shoe (least-norm tractions on its outer faces, exact force and moment); face stress = in-plane principal |sigma| at the outer-face element centroids (sigma = D B u); hot-spot = 1.67 s(0.4t) - 0.67 s(1.0t) below each shoe lower edge, max over x, both faces, both senses; ultimate = sf x limit; MS = s_face / s_ult - 1; meshes 8 mm global, 2/1/0.5 mm in the tip box; Richardson r 2

nodes.title: Station modes, 3-D solid quarters with A3 masses, 3 meshes
nodes.equation: hex8 laminate (faces, cores, strips, shoe), CF tube as an orthotropic square bar (E_z I = E I_tube, G_xz J_sq = G J_tube), rigid ties to the tube root (k_root springs), tube end, collar (brace spring k = 1/(L/EA + 1/k_anchor) at the ear); station rigid body (A3 motor 84.2 g) on the mount springs; consistent mass; eigsh shift-invert; station mode = KE share >= 0.10; meshes 8/5.7/4 mm (bar and link at half size), Richardson r sqrt 2; separation = min |f/f_forcing - 1| over 1P/2P hover/cruise and 1P max

nodes.title: 3-D gain of each station-mode lever on the governing quarter (CDR-19)
nodes.equation: first station mode of the lower quarter, hex8 model, mesh level 2 (5.7 mm), one change at a time; gain = f1(lever) / f1(base) - 1; separation with the lever = (1 + sep_3D) (1 + gain) - 1, sep_3D = CALC-C4-SIM-MODES sep_min (three meshes, extrapolated); gain needed = (1 + sep_req) / (1 + sep_3D) - 1
